epics.name: Ask a question
epics.description: Asking the chat about marine accidents in plain words and getting a clear answer back, including follow-up questions, plain maritime English, and answers that draw on every source in the database.

epics.name: Check the evidence
epics.description: Being able to trust an answer: every claim is checked against the passage it cites before it is shown, every claim links to the right page of the source report, and answers are tested against questions with known right answers.

epics.name: Spot patterns across reports
epics.description: Finding out what keeps going wrong across every report from every country: exact counts, like-for-like comparisons between countries, each accident counted once, and patterns found in report text saved and reused.

epics.name: Learn from similar incidents
epics.description: Describing an incident, near miss or task and getting back the most similar past cases and what was learned from them, including task briefings and toolbox talks built from real cases.

epics.name: Keep the data accurate
epics.description: The work that keeps the reports in the database complete, current and correctly coded: proposing and confirming SHIELD codes, loading CHIRP's own reports, and picking up newly published reports automatically.

epics.name: Account & Access
epics.description: Everything a person needs to start and keep using the chat. CHIRP staff sign in with their existing CHIRPdb accounts from Release 1. Members of the public get signing up, signing in, saved conversations, control over their own data, CHIRP's terms, and finding the chat in the first place.

epics.name: Report a problem
epics.description: Letting users flag an answer they think is wrong, and letting CHIRP staff see it with the conversation attached and withdraw the answer or the record behind it.

epics.name: Run the service safely
epics.description: Running the chat reliably and safely for staff and the public: deployment, logging every question, monitoring and backups, clear failure messages, usage limits and a spending cap on the AI bill, refusing off-topic or manipulative questions, keeping public users away from staff tools, and a closed beta before launch.

releases.name: Foundation: country ingestion
releases.target_outcome: Reports from six more countries are in CHIRPdb by fast ingestion, complete before Release 3 begins.

releases.name: Pre-release: Narrative and review triage
releases.target_outcome: 4 build days under the Statement of Work dated 18 November 2026, separate from the Tranche 2 releases. Jev checks the high-volume review items and the reviewer's queue puts what needs a person first; Zig Zag's analyst can pull the Narrative of every UK report.

releases.name: Release 1: Staff chat
releases.target_outcome: CHIRP staff can answer "how many" questions about UK marine accidents themselves, in minutes rather than by searching MAIB reports by hand. They can trust each count because it is checked against the database and links to the reports behind it.

releases.name: Release 2: Full answers
releases.target_outcome: CHIRP staff can ask what went wrong, not only how many, and get answers drawn from UK report text with every claim checked against the passage it cites. They can find past incidents similar to one they describe, get task briefings and near-miss answers, and start confirming SHIELD codes.

releases.name: Release 3: All countries
releases.target_outcome: Answers draw on reports from all eight countries plus CHIRP's own published reports. Each accident counts once however many reports describe it, new reports arrive automatically, and what the AI finds in report text is saved and reused.

releases.name: Release 4: Public access
releases.target_outcome: The chat is ready for seafarers to use safely. They can sign up, use it within limits that protect CHIRP's budget, and control their own data. CHIRP can catch and correct a wrong answer.

releases.name: Release 5: Launch
releases.target_outcome: Real seafarers have tried the chat and their most important problems are fixed. It is open to anyone, easy to find, and explains what it can and can't do.

releases.name: Backlog
releases.target_outcome: Coulds not yet placed in a release.
